errors.description: Length of the slant pocket openings. Normalised to waistband depth (80px in both images): the drawing's opening runs 385px vertically, 4.8 waistband depths, from the seam down to well below mid-thigh. The render's wearer-right opening runs about 168px (2.1 depths) and the wearer-left about 232px (2.9). Both materially short, and the two sides do not match.
errors.expected: Both slant openings running about 4.8 waistband depths from the waistband seam down and outward, terminating near the side seam
errors.actual: Openings of 2.1 and 2.9 waistband depths, fading out before the side seam and unequal side to side
errors.correction: Run each slant opening the full drawn length - from the waistband seam down and outward for about five waistband depths until it meets the side seam - and light it so the jetted lip stays legible along its whole run on both sides.

errors.description: The two pocket openings are not equally resolvable. The wearer's left opening reads clearly as a dark jetted slit; the wearer's right is a faint tonal edge only, and confirming it exists at all took effort. The drawing renders both identically.
errors.expected: Two identical equally legible slant openings, mirror-matched about centre front
errors.actual: One clearly resolved opening and one faint, shorter one
errors.correction: Light the front from a single high three-quarter source at a shallow enough angle that both jetted pocket lips throw a matching shadow line, so the two openings read with equal weight.

notes:
THE SUBSTANTIVE FIX LANDED. The absence test was applied in two parts. Part one passes outright - nothing is wrongly present. Part two now passes too, which is what failed before: the cloth moved from near-black to mid-grey giving real tonal latitude, and the light is directional from the upper left rather than flat frontal, so sheen rolls continuously across each front panel with the pressed creases as the only vertical breaks. A pleated front could not produce this reading. This is the fourth confirmation that an option whose only signal is DEPTH needs light that models depth.

The demonstration is good rather than emphatic - the light is soft-directional, not truly raking, so the modelling is gentle and a more oblique key would make the flatness undeniable.

The pocket-opening half is only partly fixed: openings are resolvable now but short against the drawing and markedly unequal between sides.

NOT measurable: any centimetre figure - no callouts, so all figures are ratios against waistband depth, read as 80px in both images. The crease start heights could not be pinned precisely; low contrast in the upper leg leaves the left crease onset uncertain within about one waistband depth, which is why that finding is minor.
